edit.find: What the strip below the boundary looks like on the world map (and whether it is the intended 'iris') is decoded from the tables, not observed.
edit.with: Measured on the world map: below the boundary row the screen is black with the BG3 text (the destination menu) on top. The screen is in Mode 1 there (BGMODE $09), BG1 and the backdrop are the colour-math layers, and the white fixed colour is subtracted from them; the FF / 01 alternation of the COLDATA fill keeps the fixed colour white on every line, because the $01 writes select no colour plane. Above the boundary row the map is Mode 7. The boundary row (151 + 2 x offset step) is off the bottom of the 224-line screen from the 37th step, so about 37 frames after the route starts the whole picture is Mode 7.

edit.find: {count 1, data word 0} plus a $00 terminator into $7E7000 (M7A), $7E7800 (M7B) and $7E8000 (M7C): 673 bytes each.
edit.with: {count 1, data word untouched} plus a $00 terminator into $7E7000 (M7A), $7E7800 (M7B) and $7E8000 (M7C): each table is 673 bytes long and the fill stores 225 of them (the 224 count bytes and the terminator). The data words are not cleared: the area is the scene loader's decompression scratch, so they hold stale bytes (measured right after the fill: 50, 54 and 38 of the 224 words are nonzero) until the first computation overwrites them (measured: the tables hold computed values within 4 frames of the fill).
(0.703 degrees per step; measured: increasing $BC turns the map clockwise on the screen)

edit.find: Not traced: whether any scene runs both.
edit.with: Measured in the four scenes that run Mode7PerspectiveUpdate ($FE world map, $8C prologue, $59 Sky Garden crash, $C0 Angkor Wat vision): after the first table fill nothing else writes $7E7000-$8FFF, and no DMA from this area runs while the scene is active. Before the fill the scene loader's decompressor (QuintetLzDecompress, the literal and back-reference stores) uses the area as scratch.

partNotes.Mode7FillTableLoop: Fill loop: one entry per scanline in all three tables (count byte 1; the data bytes are not written), 224 times, then $00 terminators.
